title: Object attribute reference with getter doesn't work as expected
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.4.1.stable

### System information

Windows 10 pro - Godot 4.4.1.stable - Nvidia GeForce GTX 1080

### Issue description

I have a class which contains a resource as an attribute.
```
extends Node2D
class_name Actor
@export var game_attributes: Resource # example: task = null
```
I also made a simple getter and setter for passing game_attributes directly to an actor object
```
func _get(property):
	if game_attributes and property in game_attributes:
		return game_attributes.get(property)
	return null

func _set(property, value):
	if game_attributes and property in game_attributes:
		game_attributes.set(property, value)
		return true
	return false
```
So, my idea is to get it like this:
`actor.task`
instead of 
`actor.game_attributes.task  `

It works in most of the cases, but HERE IS the issue begins.
1. initial task = null
2. task has been set to some Task object
3. actor.task # syntax works
4. actor.task = null # task is finished, so null
5. actor.game_attributes.task # syntax works, correctly returns the null
6. actor.task # **Invalid access to property or key 'task'** on a base object of type 'Node2D (Actor)'.

so, what i see:
+ setter on step (4) has been called, and made his job as expected (actor.game_attributes.task = null # works)
+ actor.game_attributes.task # returns null correctly
+ actor.task # getter has been called, but
- actor.task # Error happened

What is going on? May be step (4) somehow breaks the getter logic? 



### Steps to reproduce

```
extends Node2D
class_name Actor
@export var game_attributes: Resource # example: task = null

func _get(property):
	if game_attributes and property in game_attributes:
		return game_attributes.get(property)
	return null

func _set(property, value):
	if game_attributes and property in game_attributes:
		game_attributes.set(property, value)
		return true
	return false
```

```
extends Resource
@export var actor_type: String = "Human"
@export var task: Task = null
```

```
extends Resource
class_name Task
var name: String
```

```
var task = Task.new()
actor.task = task

print(actor.game_attributes.task)
print(actor.task)

# task is finished
actor.task = null

print(actor.game_attributes.task)
print(actor.task)
```
The last print will throw an **Error instead of printing <null>**
